comparison: Both evaluate MST binding data (C82-C86). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to contradiction with BLI data and acknowledged fluorescent labeling artifacts. Peer review rates as UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 strongly challenging the results and finding the fluorescent labeling explanation unconvincing, noting it should affect all mutants not just P317R.

Both evaluate BLI binding data (C92-C95). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing BLI as resolving MST discrepancies and avoiding fluorescent labeling artifacts. Peer review rates as UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 arguing BLI results are inconsistent with published literature, show poor sensorgram fits, and may be subject to artifacts.

Both evaluate structural/mechanistic hypotheses for P317R selectivity (C117-C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C117 is supported by Chowdhury et al. 2016 but remaining claims are speculative without direct experimental support. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with reviewers accepting the structural interpretation as consistent with existing data, though acknowledging lack of high-resolution structural analysis.

Both evaluate clinical characterization from case compilation (C52-C70, with peer also including C38). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing the data-driven observations and haploinsufficiency/LOH hypotheses as reasonable. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED after initial concerns about data sourcing were addressed via Supplementary file 1 reference.

Both evaluate the key NMR finding of P317R's selective NODD defect (C87-C91, C111, with peer also including C114-C116). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, calling it the central discovery with well-validated methodology. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with all reviewers recognizing this as a major finding providing solid evidence, though initial NMR methodology concerns were addressed in revision.

Both evaluate comprehensive mutant characterization including stability, structure, and enzymatic data (C7, C101-C105, C108, C122-C123, with peer also including luciferase and additional claims C71-C81, C106-C107, C109-C110). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for the synthesis across assays. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about SEC methodology (unequal loading), poor use of structural data, and unreliability of luciferase assays.

Both evaluate the major biological conclusion about NODD functional importance (C10-C11, with peer also including C50-C51). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing the logic as sound based on convergence of clinical, cellular, and biochemical data. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with editor stating it provides solid evidence and reviewers accepting the conclusion despite noting lack of in vivo validation as beyond scope.

Partial overlap on biophysical characterization (C75-C81). OpenEval R5 rates these SEC and CD data as SUPPORTED with appropriate techniques and reasonable interpretations. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation, specifically criticizing SEC methodology for unequal protein loading making data 'anecdotal rather than definitive.'

Partial overlap on luciferase assay data and reliability (C71-C72, C106-C107, C109-C110). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to internal inconsistency—if assay is unreliable, positive results are also questionable. Peer review includes these in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation, with Reviewer 3 noting 'reliance on HRE-luciferase reporter assays may not reliably reflect PHD2 function' and authors acknowledging the assay 'is not reliable.'

Minimal overlap on stability data (C73-C74). OpenEval R4 rates as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analysis showing differential stability. Peer R1 includes these in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation but does not specifically challenge the stability findings themselves.

Minimal overlap on citation of previous work (C114). OpenEval R16 rates as SUPPORTED, noting independent validation of P317R selective defect. Peer R3 includes this in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of the NMR findings, recognizing convergence of evidence.

Minimal overlap on case numbers (C38). OpenEval R1 rates clinical landscape claims as SUPPORTED based on citations and supplementary files. Peer R5 initially questioned data sourcing but accepted after Supplementary file 1 reference was clarified.

Minimal overlap on HIF dysregulation mechanism (C50). OpenEval R1 rates as SUPPORTED as well-established in field. Peer R7 rates broader biological conclusion as SUPPORTED, with editor affirming dysregulation of PHD2/HIF axis underpins erythrocytosis.

OpenEval R12 evaluates background knowledge on HIF hydroxylation and NODD significance (C3-C6, C29-C33, C112-C113), rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are established background facts framing the research question.

OpenEval R13 evaluates background from mouse genetic studies (C96-C100), rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are cited background facts providing context for PHD2 importance.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background on erythropoiesis and hypoxia response (C12-C28), rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are well-established physiological facts providing necessary context.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background on PHD2 biochemical and structural properties (C41-C46), rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found—these are cited background facts justifying focus on PHD2.
